course_summary:
ISEN 616 | Design and Analysis of Industrial Experiments | Spring 2026
Instructor: Rui Tuo | ruituo@tamu.edu
Meets: N/A | Online
Grading: Homework [10%], Exam 1 [20%], Exam 2 [20%], Final Exam [30%], Group Project [20%] — A: 90%-100%, B: 80%-89.9%, C: 70%-79.9%, D: 60%-69.9%, F: less than 60%
Topics: Taguchi methods, Latin squares, Orthogonal arrays, maximum resolution, minimum aberration, robust parameter design, 'one-factor-at-a-time' plans, optimal blocking schemes, optimal designs, full two-level factorial experiments, fractional two-level factorial experiments, fractional factorial experiments at three levels, factorial experiments at two levels, response surface methodologies, Variation reduction, analysis of location, analysis of dispersion, treatment comparison procedures, one-factor experiments with restrictions on randomization, one-factor experiments without restrictions on randomization, parameter estimation, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, statistical data analysis, model building, engineering formulations, engineering applications, industrial experimental design, fundamental principles of design, off-line experimentation techniques, design tools, industrial applications, data-collecting, experiment planning capability, product improvement, process improvement, formulations, concepts, analytical procedures
Tools: R statistical software package, Canvas, Knovel
Prerequisites: STAT 212 or STAT 601
